text:
We treat the photosphere as being in LTE, so the level populations of neutral Ti obey the Boltzmann law  

N₂/N₁ = (g₂/g₁) exp(-ΔE / kT)  

where  
• N₁ , N₂ = number of Ti I atoms in levels 1 and 2  
• ΔE = energy difference between the two levels  
• k = Boltzmann constant.

Because only the temperature changes, the statistical–weight ratio g₂/g₁ cancels when we form the ratio of the populations at the two temperatures.

1. Energy of the transition  
λ = 1448 Å = 1.448 × 10⁻⁷ m  
ΔE = hc/λ  
     = (6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)(2.998 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹) / 1.448 × 10⁻⁷ m  
     ≈ 1.372 × 10⁻¹⁸ J  
     = 1.372 × 10⁻¹⁸ J / 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J eV⁻¹  
     ≈ 8.57 eV  

2. Convert ΔE to temperature units  
ΔE/k = 8.57 eV / (8.617 × 10⁻⁵ eV K⁻¹) ≈ 9.94 × 10⁴ K

3. Ratio of excited–to–ground populations at the two temperatures  
R = (N₂/N₁)_{6000K} / (N₂/N₁)_{5500K}  
   = exp[-ΔE/k (1/6000 K – 1/5500 K)]  

   1/6000 – 1/5500 = (5500 – 6000) / (6000 × 5500)  
                    = ‑500 / 3.3 × 10⁷  
                    = ‑1.515 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹  

   Therefore  
   R = exp[(9.94 × 10⁴ K)(1.515 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)]  
     ≈ exp(1.51)  
     ≈ 4.5

So the excited-to-ground level population ratio at 6000 K is about 4.5 times larger than at 5500 K.

Since observers said the ratio decreases when the star has spots (cooler), we have confirmed the expected direction.

The closest choice is:

(D) ~4.5

Answer: D
